title: Asymmetric Class Sourcing Creates Provenance Confounds in Authenticity-Classification Image Datasets: code and analysis pipeline

creators.name: Zhu, Sophie
creators.affiliation: Mira Costa High School, Manhattan Beach, CA, USA

description:
Code, data pipeline and manuscript sources for a study of class-conditional provenance confounding: when the two classes of an authenticity-classification image dataset are sourced by different procedures, the label predicts the acquisition process rather than the property being labeled, and no in-distribution evaluation can detect it.

Contains the full data pipeline (filtering, rotation-aware perceptual-hash de-duplication, product-grouped splits), four model families, external evaluation on two independently captured distributions, a label-free normalization operator ablated per axis, per architecture, per constant and per composition order, calibration and attention audits, and a provenance audit run across four application areas from public dataset file listings.

This archive contains no images. The case-study archive carries no license grant, so no image from it is redistributed — only derived per-image statistics, split assignments and filenames. All image-derived artifacts are regenerated by the committed scripts from a user's own copy of the source archives.
